audit_items.title: Is Bloom returned only after all logs are fully processed?
audit_items.skip_detail: Prysm is a Consensus Layer (CL) client. Bloom computation from logs is an Execution Layer (EL) operation performed by the EL client (e.g., geth). Prysm only stores LogsBloom as an opaque 256-byte field in ExecutionPayload protobuf messages (proto/engine/v1/execution_engine.pb.go:93) and does not compute or validate bloom filters. All EL-specific validation is delegated to the execution engine via the Engine API.

code_scope.note: EL property - not implemented in Prysm CL client

audit_items.skip_detail: Receipt bloom consistency verification is an EL operation. Prysm (CL client) stores ReceiptsRoot and LogsBloom as opaque bytes in ExecutionPayload (proto/engine/v1/execution_engine.pb.go:92-93) and does not verify bloom-to-log consistency. This validation occurs inside the EL client during block execution.

audit_items.skip_detail: EIP-7934 RLP block size limits are an EL-level concern. Prysm (CL client) handles blocks via SSZ encoding, not RLP. Block size limits at the EL level are enforced by the EL client. Prysm does enforce blob commitment limits per slot (beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go:verifyBlobCommitmentCount) but not EL RLP size limits.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is parent_hash validated against canonical chain?
audit_items.skip_detail: While Prysm does validate payload.parent_hash == state.latest_execution_payload_header.block_hash in ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes (beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go:129-141), this is a CL-level check against the latest execution payload header stored in beacon state. The EL-level check of parent_hash against the canonical EL chain is performed by the EL client. The checklist item refers to the EL-level canonical chain validation, which is outside Prysm's scope.

code_scope.note: EL-level canonical chain validation - not implemented in Prysm CL client. Prysm performs CL-level parent_hash consistency check only.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is timestamp > parent.timestamp enforced?
audit_items.skip_detail: EL-level timestamp ordering (timestamp > parent.timestamp) is an EL block validation rule. Prysm (CL client) validates that payload.timestamp == compute_timestamp_at_slot(state, state.slot) in ValidatePayload (beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go:165-167), which is a different CL-level check. The EL-level parent timestamp ordering check is performed by the EL client.

code_scope.note: EL property - Prysm checks timestamp matches slot, not parent ordering

No patricialize, trie_set, or MPT-related functions exist in the Prysm codebase. This property applies to EL state management (geth, execution specs).
